title: Come Home
teaser: Three years gone. One message from a number you don't know.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three years. That's how long you've been gone from Harborview.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tonight your phone lit up with a message from a number you didn't know.

lines.speaker: unknown
lines.text: Come home. Maya needs you. Tell no one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You were on the last train within the hour.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The platform is empty except for one figure under the lamp, holding a notebook over their head against the rain.

lines.speaker: jun
lines.text: Well. Look what the tide dragged in.

lines.speaker: jun
lines.text: I'm at the Herald now. All four pages of it. So you know I have to ask.

lines.speaker: jun
lines.text: What brings you back after three years?

choices.text: Someone sent me a message. They said Maya needs me.

response.speaker: jun
response.text: Maya? Huh.

response.speaker: jun
response.text: Don't worry. I won't print it. Probably.

choices.text: Just visiting. It felt like time.

response.speaker: jun
response.text: Sure. And I'm just here for the weather.

choices.text: Not tonight, Jun.

response.speaker: jun
response.text: Fair. The Herald can wait.

response.speaker: jun
response.text: Welcome home, anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Morning. Rosa's café still smells like burnt sugar and sea salt.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Sit. You look like you slept on a train.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: You're here about Maya. Don't make that face. Everyone's here about Maya, eventually.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: She hasn't been in for a week. Ten years, and she's never missed a Tuesday.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Daniel says she's just tired. Wedding nerves.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: And Jun was in here at seven telling anyone who'd listen that you got a 'mysterious message.'

scenes.prompt: Rosa refills your cup without asking.

choices.text: Where can I find her?

response.speaker: rosa
response.text: Same blue house by the harbor. Knock twice. She won't answer once.

choices.text: Wedding? Since when is Maya marrying Daniel?

response.speaker: rosa
response.text: Since spring. You'd know if you'd called.

response.speaker: rosa
response.text: Blue house by the harbor. Go.

choices.text: Has anyone else been asking about her?

response.speaker: rosa
response.text: Funny you say that. Daniel was in here last month, asking whether you'd ever come back.

response.speaker: rosa
response.text: I told him nobody comes back to Harborview. And then here you are.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The blue house. The paint is peeling now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You knock twice.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I didn't expect you to come back.

scenes.prompt: Maya doesn't open the door any wider.

choices.text: I came back because of you.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: You don't get to say that. Not after three years.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Come in before the neighbors see.

choices.text: I had unfinished business.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: That makes two of us. Come in.

choices.text: Maybe I shouldn't have come back.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Maybe.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: But you're here now. Come in.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I didn't send it. Whatever you got. I don't even have your number anymore.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: But I got one too. Last week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She holds out her phone.

lines.speaker: unknown
lines.text: He knows what you did. Stay quiet and it stays buried.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And don't tell Eli. He'll do something stupid. He always does.

scenes.prompt: Maya waits for you to say something.

choices.text: What did you do, Maya?

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Something I'm not ready to talk about. Not even with you.

choices.text: Whatever it is, I'm here.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: That's what you said last time.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: But… thank you.

choices.text: Give me the phone. I'll find who sent it.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Fine. I doubt it'll do you any good.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You barely reach the end of the pier before someone grabs your arm.

lines.speaker: eli
lines.text: Stay away from my sister.

lines.speaker: eli
lines.text: Last time you left, she didn't leave the house for a month. I'm not watching that again.

lines.speaker: eli
lines.text: She's scared of something. I know she is. What did she tell you?

scenes.prompt: Eli wants to know what Maya told you.

choices.text: She got a message. Someone's threatening her.

response.speaker: eli
response.text: Threatening her? Who?

response.speaker: eli
response.text: Never mind. I already know who.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: He's gone before you can stop him.

choices.text: Nothing. We just talked about old times.

response.speaker: eli
response.text: You're a bad liar. You always were.

response.speaker: eli
response.text: Fine. Keep her secrets. Just don't leave this time.

choices.text: She told me to leave town. So I'm leaving.

response.speaker: eli
response.text: …Good.

response.speaker: eli
response.text: Look. If you're leaving anyway. I've seen Daniel's car at the old lighthouse. Midnight, three nights running.

response.speaker: eli
response.text: Don't tell her I said that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel has a fresh red mark across his jaw. He doesn't mention it.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: There they are. The one who got away.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Jun tells me you got a mysterious message. Exciting stuff, for a town like this.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Maya's fine, by the way. In case you were wondering. Just tired.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: So. What brings you back?

scenes.prompt: Daniel's smile doesn't reach his eyes.

choices.text: Visiting old friends.

response.speaker: daniel
response.text: Of course. Don't stay too long. Harborview has a way of keeping people.

choices.text: Someone's threatening Maya. Know anything about that?

response.speaker: daniel
response.text: Threatening? That's a serious word.

response.speaker: daniel
response.text: Careful who you say it to. People here talk.

choices.text: Congratulations on the engagement.

response.speaker: daniel
response.text: That's generous of you. Really.

response.speaker: daniel
response.text: She talks about you, you know. Less than she used to.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The old lighthouse hasn't been lit in years. Mr. Hale still climbs it every evening anyway.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Thought you'd turn up. The tide always brings things back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fresh tire tracks in the gravel. Eli was right about the car.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Messages, is it? Words travel strange in this town. Somebody always wants a thing said, and somebody else wants it buried.

scenes.prompt: Hale studies you over his pipe.

choices.text: Did you send it, Mr. Hale?

response.speaker: hale
response.text: Me? I don't even own one of those telephones.

response.speaker: hale
response.text: But I know someone's been using the old one in the keeper's office. Late at night.

choices.text: Who gains if I come home?

response.speaker: hale
response.text: Now that's the right question.

response.speaker: hale
response.text: Someone who needs a stranger to dig up what they can't touch themselves.

choices.text: I don't have time for riddles.

response.speaker: hale
response.text: Then you'll soon have time for nothing else.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By evening the whole town has heard. Eli walked into the town hall and hit Daniel in front of half the council.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I asked you for one thing. One.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Eli's in a cell overnight, and now Daniel gets to be the victim. Do you understand what you've done?

choices.text: He had a right to know.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Maybe. But it wasn't your choice to make.

choices.text: Then let me fix it.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: You can't fix this town. Nobody can.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Evening. Maya is waiting on the porch steps.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Eli came by. He said you didn't tell him anything.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: He's furious with you. I'm… not.

scenes.prompt: She makes room for you on the step.

choices.text: He'll come around.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: He won't. But thank you for trying.

choices.text: Maya. What did the message mean?

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Tomorrow. I'll tell you tomorrow. I promise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Evening. Maya is waiting on the porch steps.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Eli says you're leaving town.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: You lied to him. Didn't you?

scenes.prompt: There's no anger in it. Just tiredness.

choices.text: I did. He was about to do something stupid.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: …He was. Thank you.

choices.text: He told me Daniel's been at the lighthouse at midnight.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: The lighthouse?

response.speaker: maya
response.text: That's where… no. Not yet. I can't.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It's late. You could stay.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: On the couch. Before you get ideas.

scenes.prompt: The harbor lights go out, one by one.

choices.text: I'll stay.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Couch. I meant it.

choices.text: I'll walk the harbor. Someone should keep watch.

response.speaker: maya
response.text: Be careful. This town is smaller than it looks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Past midnight, your phone lights up.

lines.speaker: unknown
lines.text: You told someone. That was a mistake.

lines.speaker: unknown
lines.text: Now it's my turn.

lines.speaker: unknown
lines.text: Good. You kept quiet.

lines.speaker: unknown
lines.text: Lighthouse. Tomorrow. Midnight. Come alone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the water, a light flickers at the top of the dead lighthouse. Once. Twice. Then dark.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the room, Maya's phone buzzes at the very same moment. She doesn't wake.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: To be continued…

outcomes.title: The Fallout
outcomes.text: You told Eli the truth. He did exactly what Maya feared, and now the whole town has a story, and Daniel has a reason.

outcomes.title: The Useful Lie
outcomes.text: You lied to Eli, and he handed you something real in return. Somewhere, someone is keeping count of your lies.

outcomes.title: The Shield
outcomes.text: You kept Maya's secret, even from her brother. She trusts you a little more. Eli doesn't trust you at all.

reflections.text: Maya is starting to let you back in.
Maya is keeping you at arm's length.
People are beginning to believe what you tell them.
Harborview is talking about you, and not kindly.
Jun didn't print it. Jun didn't need to.
Maya's phone is in your pocket. You haven't looked yet.

s_daniel_asked.title: Daniel was waiting
s_daniel_asked.text: A month before the message, Daniel asked Rosa whether you'd ever come back.

s_stolen.title: Something stolen
s_stolen.text: STEAL, hidden in Rosa's napkin. The week Maya stopped coming in, the journal she kept behind the counter went missing.

s_reset.title: Wiped clean
s_reset.text: RESET, scratched into the lighthouse rail. Someone wiped Maya's phone the night the messages began.

m_return.title: Last Train Home
m_return.text: Rain on the platform, and Jun under the only lamp.

m_cafe.title: Rosa's Corner Table
m_cafe.text: Burnt sugar, sea salt, and a cup you didn't ask for.

m_door.title: The Blue Door
m_door.text: "I didn't expect you to come back."

m_lighthouse.title: The Dark Lighthouse
m_lighthouse.text: It hasn't been lit in years. Somebody still climbs it.

m_message.title: Past Midnight
m_message.text: A second message, and the whole town asleep.
